Subject: Post-demo recap: tenant isolation & reserved GPU plan for OrionBio

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap while it's fresh and proposed next steps so we can move toward a reserved capacity proposal.

Summary of pain / goals (from our call)
- Production latency spikes during peak inference (esp. long-context document parsing).
- Strict data isolation requirement for PHI workflows; customer must ensure isolated GPU tenancy for compliance.
- Predictable throughput for nightly batch jobs and daytime interactive sessions (mixed load).
- Need a path to burst for short-term campaign peaks without losing isolation guarantees.

What we recommend as an initial presizing (subject to telemetry/POC):
- Dedicated pool (Reserved) with isolation: 6 x A100-80GB equivalent (baseline) to meet steady-state throughput and KV cache sizes.
- Burst capacity: policy to autoscale/burst up to 12 GPUs into a private tenant pool for 2–6 hour peaks (can be metered + throttled).
- SLA targets we can commit to in proposal: 99th percentile per-request latency <= 500ms for typical generation paths; availability SLA 99.9% for the reserved pool.
- Deployment: Private control plane + VPC peering (or on-prem option later) for audit/logging and KMS integration.

Open questions we promised to clarify
- Exact peak concurrent requests and average tokens per request (you mentioned 3–4k tokens on some jobs).
- Any hard regulatory requirement for data residency (region-specific long-term storage).
- Procurement cadence (PO / SOW timing).

Immediate next steps
1) Your team: confirm expected peak concurrent requests and a representative nightly batch job window (start/end times).
2) Our infra: Ben will validate the presizing and provide an ops playbook draft and cost ballpark.
3) Contracts/procurement: Lauren to introduce Redwood contracting options and timeline.
4) We'll schedule a short technical sizing call (30m) to review KV cache expectations and sample prompt lengths — propose Tue 2026-08-25 10:00 PT.

Attachments: demo slide deck (attached), sample MOP template.

Thanks — I'll hold the slot tentatively until I hear back.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful and captures the ask. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak profile: expect sustained ~75 concurrent interactive sessions during product hours with occasional spikes up to ~200 concurrent (10–15 minute spikes). Nightly batch: heavy window between 02:00–05:00 PT processing ~1.2M tokens over the window.
- Typical request size: 2k–4k tokens (most fall around 2.5k).
- Data residency: US-only for now, but audit logs must be retained for 7 years (we'll share retention spec).
- Isolation: Dedicated tenancy is mandatory for any environment that processes PHI. We can accept VPC + reserved pool if Redwood can provide KMS/HSM key controls for customer-managed keys.

Questions:
1) How fast is burst provisioning? Can we rely on scheduled autoscale to guarantee availability for predictable marketing campaign spikes?
2) Do you support canary rollouts that keep a subset of requests on current model variants for quality guardrails during big rollouts?

I've attached a short compliance notes doc that lists the retention and logging fields we care about. We'll confirm procurement timing by Friday.

Appreciate the suggested timeslot for the technical sizing call — Tue 08/25 10:00 PT works for Priya and me.

Best,
Alex Green
CTO, OrionBio

Karthik — ran the initial presize with infra and ops. Short summary:

Recommendation (initial, conservative presize)
- Baseline reserved pool: 6 x A100-80GB equivalents (dedicated tenant); supports ~80–100 sustained concurrent short-generation sessions (2–3k tokens) with CAche sizing for long-context workloads.
- Burst policy: scheduled autoscale (pre-warmed) up to 12 GPUs. We recommend scheduled burst windows for marketing campaigns; unscheduled instantaneous provisioning can be slower (10–30 minutes) depending on available capacity in the region.
- Latency expectations: 95th pctl < 220ms for short generations; 99th pctl expected <= 480ms on heavier long-context paths (these are our internal run numbers and will be validated in a POC).
- SLA: proposed 99.9% uptime for the reserved tenant; we can include an operations runbook and fallback routing to a secondary idle pool for emergency failover.

Ops notes
- KV cache sizing: we recommend a shared prefix cache strategy within the tenant to reduce per-token compute during repeated document parsing. We'll size after we see sample prompts (please forward a redacted example).
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations; legal will need the key rotation and access control language in the SOW.

Next commercial steps
1) Sizing call tomorrow 2026-08-25 10:00 PT to confirm KV cache and sample prompt lengths (we've accepted the calendar invite).
2) I'll prepare a non-binding cost sheet (capacity_sku_pricing.pdf) and an ops playbook draft by EOD Wed 2026-08-26.
3) Lauren — once procurement gives target PO date, we can align on an SOW + reserved capacity term (12-month vs 24-month commit) and discounting bands.

I'll attach the preliminary pricing doc and a short ops checklist.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
